To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we present the first system that allows a domain scientist to perform complex scientific tasks in a problem-specific way; (ii) we present a system that supports the creation of workflows in a domain-specific way; (iii) we present a workflow system that supports both the creation of workflows and the execution of workflows as Web services.
(i) we can build a system that supports complex, problem specific, scientific workflows; and (ii) the system is used to solve a complex, real-world problem by a domain scientist.
we have developed a system that allows scientists to create and execute complex workflows that involve both data access, querying and manipulation as well as computation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated environment for the modeling, execution, and sharing of complex, distributed scientific workflows.
providing the scientific community with a new generation of Web-based tools for performing distributed data and knowledge-intensive tasks.

the development of a modeling, analysis, and execution environment for scientific workflows that are distributed, heterogeneous, and Web-enabled, and that are based on the Web services model of computation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system is an important step in making scientific workflows more usable by the scientific community at large.
our system provides a modeling environment that supports the creation of complex workflows, which can be executed as Web services.
the system is an important step toward the vision of a "virtual lab" where scientists can perform complex tasks in an integrated environment, using the best available tools and data sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a framework for the modeling and execution of scientific workflows, which is both flexible and powerful enough to support the needs of a wide range of scientific domains, while at the same time being simple to use.
it is the first system that allows a scientist to perform a complex scientific analysis task by interlinking computations, data and queries from several sources, in a problem specific, complex way.
we have created a modeling and execution environment that allows domain scientists to express and execute complex, problem specific workflows that involve data and computations from multiple sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have demonstrated the feasibility of a system that supports scientists in the execution of complex, multi-step, scientific tasks by interlinking computations and data from several sources, local and remote, in a transparent and seamless way.
the use of Web services and the Semantic Web technologies can be used in a synergistic way to provide a flexible and easy-to-use system for scientific data analysis.

the Web can be used as a platform for scientific computing and data access, and that it is possible to build a system that supports the scientist in performing complex scientific tasks by combining data, computation, and analysis in a seamless manner.
